keys.description: Where pseudonymisation keys live. Unset, or `none`, means no pseudonyms, no key material and no resolve.

dir.description: Where the wrapped data keys are kept. They are random, not derived, so this directory is the only copy; unset keeps them in memory, which a trial install may do and nothing else should.

rootFile.description: A file holding the 32-byte root the data keys are wrapped under.

prefix.description: What every key's name starts with: <prefix>.<purpose>.<tenant>.

openbao.description: How a process reaches an OpenBAO transit engine: where it is, and exactly one way of signing in.

caFile.description: A PEM bundle trusted beside the system roots, for a server on a private chain.

login.description: Sign in with a JWT: the pod's projected service-account token, presented to an auth mount. Nothing is stored.

jwtFile.description: The file holding the JWT, read at every login because the kubelet replaces a projected token before it expires.

mount.description: The JWT auth mount, for example jwt-devel.
Where the transit engine is mounted.

namespace.description: The OpenBAO namespace the engine and the auth mount are in. Unset is the root namespace.

tokenEnv.description: The NAME of the environment variable holding a token.

tokenFile.description: A file holding a token, read on every call, for a token something else keeps renewed.

postgres.description: A PostgreSQL connection. The URL carries no password: a password in it is refused, and `passwordEnv` names the environment variable that holds it.

description: The configuration of audit-writer, the installation's front door and write path. Secrets are never in this file: a field named ...Env holds the NAME of the environment variable that holds the secret. Telemetry is the OTEL_* environment, not configuration.

anonymousWrites.description: Accept writes over HTTP from callers nobody verified, stamped with no observer. For a trial install only.

archive.description: Where the archive is and how it is written.

kmsKey.description: The key objects are encrypted with. Unset uses the bucket's default encryption, which a deployment should still be setting.

lockMode.description: The Object Lock mode every object is written in: compliance (the record tier), governance (a lock a privileged role can shorten), or none (the attested tier, for a store without Object Lock). A process refuses to start when a profile demands a stricter mode than this.

prefix.description: The prefix within the bucket. Required in a bucket shared with other installations: it is what keeps two of them apart.

catalogues.description: A directory of catalogues to register at start-up.

consume.description: What a writer reads its records from, beside its own sink: exactly one of `nats` and `sqs`.

nats.description: A NATS JetStream stream; what `stream` says.

ackWait.description: How long the stream waits for a batch to be taken before offering it again. It must exceed `roll.interval` plus the longest a put can take.

batch.description: How many records are taken from the stream at once.

consumer.description: The durable consumer this installation's writers share.

sqs.description: An SQS queue the writer consumes. Credentials are never in the file: the process uses the SDK's ambient ones, which on Kubernetes is the pod's workload identity (EKS Pod Identity or IRSA) bound through the service account.

batch.description: How many messages are received at once, one to ten.

fifo.description: The queue is FIFO. It must agree with the URL, which ends in `.fifo` for one. A FIFO queue absorbs a repeated record itself, inside its five-minute window; a standard queue relies on the writer's deduplication.

region.description: The queue's region. Unset is the SDK's: AWS_REGION, which EKS Pod Identity and IRSA set.

visibility.description: How long a received message is hidden from other consumers while the writer writes it. It must outlast the write, or the message is delivered twice.

database.description: The index and the shared deduplication table. Without it the writer indexes nothing, deduplicates in process, and may only run one replica.

deployment.description: Path to the profile configuration: which presets each profile is composed from.

forgetIdentities.description: Do not keep the identity behind each pseudonym, sealed under its key. By default it is kept, so that resolve can find it.

forward.description: Where a receiver sends what it took: exactly one of `nats`, `sqs` and `log`. `log` is allowed only with `require: logged`.

log.description: The log sink: one JSON line per record on standard output, which survives nothing but the log pipeline. Nothing to configure.

nats.description: A NATS JetStream stream; what `stream` says.

ackWait.description: How long the stream waits for a batch to be taken before offering it again. It must exceed `roll.interval` plus the longest a put can take.

batch.description: How many records are taken from the stream at once.

consumer.description: The durable consumer this installation's writers share.

sqs.description: An SQS queue the receiver publishes to. Credentials are never in the file: the process uses the SDK's ambient ones, which on Kubernetes is the pod's workload identity (EKS Pod Identity or IRSA) bound through the service account.

fifo.description: The queue is FIFO. It must agree with the URL, which ends in `.fifo` for one. A FIFO queue absorbs a repeated record itself, inside its five-minute window; a standard queue relies on the writer's deduplication.

region.description: The queue's region. Unset is the SDK's: AWS_REGION, which EKS Pod Identity and IRSA set.

mode.description: `writer` serves the sink, writes the archive and consumes the stream when there is one. `receiver` serves the sink and publishes to the stream and nothing else: it holds no archive and no keys, because a receiver holding either would be a writer.

replicas.description: How many writers share this stream. Above one it needs a database, and with local keys a directory every replica shares.

require.description: The weakest durability this process's chain may give. Unset is `archived` for a writer and `queued` for a receiver. At start-up the process refuses to run if what it is configured with can never give that: a receiver, which holds no archive, cannot promise `archived`, and `forward.log` cannot promise more than `logged`. A write acknowledged weaker than this fails. See ADR 0017.

roll.description: How much a writer gathers from the stream before it writes, which decides how many objects a day of records becomes.

interval.description: How long gathered records wait before they are written, and how long an object stays open within one write.

maxRecords.description: How many gathered records are written at once.

stream.description: The wide stream, as the NATS shorthand: for a receiver it is `forward.nats`, for a writer `consume.nats`. Give it or the longhand, not both.

ackWait.description: How long the stream waits for a batch to be taken before offering it again. It must exceed `roll.interval` plus the longest a put can take.

batch.description: How many records are taken from the stream at once.

consumer.description: The durable consumer this installation's writers share.

workloads.description: Path to the file naming the issuers trusted to say which workload is publishing, and which source each speaks for. Exactly one of `workloads` and `anonymousWrites`.

title: audit-writer
